central_question: What will be the state of the US trading system by end-2028, including the effective tariff rate (ETR), the durability of the post-SCOTUS Section 232/122/301 patchwork, the trajectory of US-China/USMCA/EU trade relationships, and the role of AI-driven reshoring vs. export controls?

situation_brief.current_situation: After the 20 February 2026 SCOTUS ruling in Learning Resources v. Trump (6-3) invalidated IEEPA-based reciprocal and drug-trafficking tariffs, the effective US tariff rate fell from a 2025 peak near 16% to ~7.0% (Wharton, 16 June 2026) but has been rebuilt via Section 122 (10-15% global surcharge imposed 24 February 2026, capped at 150 days), expanded Section 232 (50% high-metal content, 25% derivatives, 15% floor; 100% on patented pharmaceuticals effective April 2026 with UK carve-out at 10%; 25% on high-end AI chips since January 2026), and surviving Section 301 actions against China (Lists 1-3 at 25%, List 4A at 7.5%). Yale Budget Lab's pre-substitution ETR reached 11.8% by 8 April 2026, the highest since the early 1940s. The US declined to renew USMCA on 1 July 2026, triggering annual joint reviews rather than collapse. CBP is processing a $166-175B IEEPA refund pool across roughly 330,000 importers and 53 million entries, with ~$90B accepted and ~$24B transmitted by 26 June 2026.
situation_brief.context: The 2025 'Liberation Day' IEEPA tariffs pushed the ETR to its highest level since 1947. Court losses culminating in the February 2026 SCOTUS ruling ended the IEEPA legal basis and triggered a $166-175B refund obligation. The administration pivoted to a three-pillar Plan B: Section 232 sectoral expansions (legally resilient since the 1980s), Section 122 (statutorily capped at 150 days, lapsing 24 July 2026 absent Congressional extension), and Section 301 buildout (60 countries under forced-labor investigation as of 12 March 2026, with USTR findings on 2 June 2026 setting 12.5% on 46 countries and 10% on 14 others). Fiscal sustainability now depends on $1.3-1.9T in 10-year tariff revenue (Yale), while the household burden is estimated at $2,000-2,800/year (Yale Budget Lab) or $1,200-1,500/year if only Section 122 is extended (Tax Foundation).
situation_brief.dynamics: Six forces are in tension: (i) judicial constraint versus executive trade ambition following the major-questions doctrine application; (ii) a dormant House tariff-rebellion caucus (Don Bacon R-NE et al.) versus Trump-aligned leadership and a Senate CRA precedent that swings the Section 122 cliff; (iii) the legal durability of Section 232/301 versus the political volatility of Section 122's 24 July 2026 expiry; (iv) US tariff-revenue needs versus trading-partner retaliation and US export-competitiveness erosion; (v) industrial-policy reshoring via CHIPS Act disbursements versus comparative advantage and Mexican nearshoring (Mexico FDI hit a record $40.87B in 2025); (vi) AI-driven productivity gains (hyperscaler capex ~$700-830B in 2026, 75% AI-directed) versus export controls strangling the PRC chip-customer base that historically funded US R&D. The administration's parallel Section 301 buildout is consistent with planning around the Section 122 lapse rather than fighting for extension.
fault_lines: Constitutional boundary of presidential tariff authority after the 6-3 SCOTUS ruling; scope of 'clear delegation' under IEEPA, Section 232, and Section 122
Section 122 cliff on 24 July 2026 — Trump/Lutnick/Greer pushing extension versus House Bacon-led rebels letting it lapse versus a parallel Section 301 buildout as substitute
USMCA renewal status — USTR Greer's 'non-renewal + annual reviews' framework versus Canada/Mexico preference for status quo and the USITC 2027 auto rules-of-origin report

CHIPS Act continuity under reported NIST restructuring and inter-agency cuts threatening disbursement timelines, with TSMC Arizona 2nm localization (per Taiwan MOEA clearance) and Intel ownership uncertainty as open variables

Export-control depth on China versus Gulf sovereign AI buyers — BIS 31 May 2026 Blackwell-loophole closure and 7 April 2026 Approved IC Designer extension to 31 December 2026 versus the 20 November 2025 BIS approval of 35,000 Nvidia GB300 equivalents each to UAE G42 and Saudi Humain
WTO reform and Appellate Body restart — DG Okonjo-Iweala's MPIA 'bridge' framing at MC14 Yaoundé (March 2026) versus continuous US veto since December 2019
